stories.title: Cardinals QB Carson Beck dealing with back spasms; Josh Johnson may start
stories.summary: The Cardinals are preparing veteran quarterback Josh Johnson to start Sunday vs. the Chiefs as rookie Carson Beck deals with back spasms, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday.
stories.detail: TEMPE, Ariz. -- The Cardinals are preparing veteran quarterback Josh Johnson to start Sunday in Kansas City as rookie Carson Beck deals with back spasms, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday. Beck is dealing with the same back issue that's been lingering all season and it "just kind of flared up," LaFleur said. Beck will not practice Friday, the second straight day he will have missed practice. However, LaFleur isn't closing the door on the possibility of Beck playing. "Just taking it one minute at a time right now, not even one day at a time, taking one minute," LaFleur said. "It's basically just kind of responding to the treatment, see how he feels when he wakes up tomorrow." LaFleur doesn't think Beck's injury will keep him out multiple weeks but said, "I can't go there yet." Beck has been preparing like he typically does, LaFleur said, in the event he's able to play. LaFleur expressed some unhappiness with not being able to see Beck continue as Arizona's starter for a second straight week. "I'd be lying to you if I said that would be OK not seeing him go on Sunday, but it is what it is," LaFleur said. "Show goes on this league. I mean, this ball's getting put down at noon on Sunday …

stories.detail: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Outside of Dallas dropping their game to the 49ers, a lot went right for the Cowboys in Week 10. We need that to keep going for the rest of the season, both for the NFC East contention and our admittedly razor-thin hopes of a Plan B in the wild card race. A Cowboys upset over San Francisco sure would’ve been nice given how other games unfolded. The Giants getting upset by the Commanders and Green Bay getting crushed at home by Minnesota were not expected. These results helped keep a division title and the seventh seed in range, one of which is required for Dallas to still get into the playoffs. Granted, that NFC East crown is far more reachable than a wild card spot. stories.title: What is fan confidence after the Puka Nacua injury?
stories.summary: Fan confidence in the Rams was looking good, now Puka Nacua is really out
stories.detail: Puka Nacua is expected to be out for the next two months , essentially ending his 2026 season, and the news should be a major blow in confidence among the team and their fanbase. The Rams went into the year as favorites to win the Super Bowl by plenty of betting sites , and talking heads. Heading into their Week 11 bye and Week 12 matchup against the Green Bay Packers before Thanksgiving, the Rams don’t look as promising. A survey was posted this week, and by its conclusion it had over 60% of Rams fans expressing confidence that L.A. was headed in the right direction. Knowing what we know about Nacua now, is confidence still high? If almost 36% of fans were concerned before L.A. essentially lost their best offensive player for the year, how many more fans are concerned now? The only thing at this point that will give the fans any faith, is a win over the Packers on Wednesday. A loss , and the season isn’t over, but it would be on life support. A win, and perhaps even with the Nacua news, fans might still believe that L.A. is headed in the right direction, and on track towards the playoffs or more. teamStories.detail: If the Raiders wanted to ease Fernando Mendoza into his new job, they have a peculiar way of showing it. First came the Seahawks, who turned his starting debut into a chess match with consequences. Six times, those consequences involved Mendoza being dropped to the ground with the ball still in his hands. Next up are the Broncos, rested from their bye and waiting in Denver. After that, the Browns in Cleveland. It is difficult to imagine a much more treacherous introduction to professional quarterbacking. Three defenses capable of making experienced quarterbacks uncomfortable, with the last two getting the rookie in their own buildings. Fernando Mendoza #15 and Cody White #82 of the Las Vegas Raiders warm up at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. The Seahawks won 21-13. Getty Images The schedule will eventually offer something more forgiving. For now, Mendoza is getting an education that requires an ice bath afterward. And somewhere down the road, he might appreciate it. The disguised coverages, the pressure arriving from unexpected places, the difference between what a defense shows before the snap and what it becomes afterward. Every uncomfortable experience …

teamStories.detail: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks managed to get six sacks on Fernando Mendoza in his starting debut last week , and pressure on the quarterback will be another major key to the game for the Las Vegas Raiders’ offense in Week 11. The Denver Broncos present the same problem but in a different way than Seattle, one that will place a greater emphasis on the Raiders’ offensive line, especially tackles Kolton Miller and DJ Glaze . Led by head coach Mike Macdonald, the Seahawks defense uses a creative scheme to help manufacture pressure and create confusion for opposing quarterbacks. To a certain extent, they’re able to work around or neutralize the offensive line by attacking running backs in pass protection or forcing quarterbacks to account for free rushers by throwing hot. Last week was a perfect example, as top cornerback Devon Witherspoon led the team with two of the six sacks. Meanwhile, Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph isn’t afraid to blitz, but that’s to help create one-on-one opportunities for their defensive linemen, especially edge rushers Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper. stories.title: Caleb Wilson's hand injuries not connected as Bulls rookie deals with 'bad luck'
stories.summary: Caleb Wilson has sustained three hand-related injuries in the past year, but the Chicago Bulls rookie said doctors told him they're not connected and that it's a case of "bad luck," he told reporters before his team's game against the Washington Wizards.
stories.detail: CHICAGO -- Caleb Wilson has sustained three hand-related injuries in the past year, but the Chicago Bulls rookie said doctors told him the injuries aren't connected. "No, it's just bad luck," Wilson said before Friday's game against the Washington Wizards . "I'm pretty healthy. I do what I'm supposed to do. I drink my milk. So sometimes you just have a bad go at things." Wilson fractured his right hand during a game on Nov. 12 when he tried to knock the ball out of Victor Wembanyama's hands. He said he knew instantly -- because he heard the break. "I looked down at my hand, and it was bent the wrong way," he said. At North Carolina last season, Wilson missed the NCAA tournament after he needed surgery to repair a broken right thumb. He also missed six games during the regular season with a broken bone in his left hand. But Wilson said each injury was a freak accident. He wore a red-and-black sling on his right hand as he spoke to the media Friday and said he has been able to continue running and do some dribbling with his left hand. The Bulls begin a three-game homestand Friday and have nine of their next 10 games at home, so although Wilson might not travel with the team while he…
